sources.title: Research
sources.text: Home Research People Publications CV Contact Home Research People Publications CV Contact Home Research People Publications CV Contact RESEARCH My work focuses on studying disease relevant proteins in as close to physiological conditions as possible. We pursue new and exciting biophysics and focus on answering questions not specific techniques. Despite being trained as an NMR spectroscopist, I am passionate about being a jack of all trades and picking the best technique to address the question at hand. Glycan targeting Antiviral design During the Covid-19 Pandemic, Alex became interested in the biophysical and mechanistic principles of glycan targeting antiviral molecules such as microbial lectins. The Guseman lab combines biophysical and virological experiments to understand the principles of glycan recognition and the mechanisms of glycan targeting antivirals. Advancements in 19F BioNMR and its applications to physiologically relevant biophysics and In-cell NMR We are frequent practitioners of in-cell NMR and physiologically relevant biophysics, where we look for new systems and methods to study how crowding and physiologically relevant environments influence proteins biophysics Biophysical basis of protein glycan interactions: In order to make new antivirals, we have found ourselves needing to define the molecular grammar of protein glycan interactions. We study how glycans are recognized by proteins in the context of specificity, affinity, and avidity as well as develop new tools to study specific glycan structures in biological systems. ​
